description: A low, matting evergreen heath of the subalpine meadows and snow basins, 10-40 cm tall, its stems crowded with short, needle-like dark-green leaves. In July and August it covers itself in small, rose-pink, bell-shaped flowers that nod at the tips of the stems.

season_notes.winter: Under deep snow until June or July, which protects it from the cold.
season_notes.spring: Melts out green and unharmed as the snowbanks retreat.
season_notes.summer: Pink bells cluster at the stem tips for a few weeks in July and August, buzzing with bumblebees.
season_notes.fall: Dry seed capsules on red stalks; the leaves stay green.

notes: Grown from the red mountain heather record (itself generated from Sierra gooseberry), the same genus and mat form. Leaves linear, 8-16 mm (Burke), drawn as lanceolate cards; flowers pink to deep rose, bell-shaped, about 7 mm, from the upper leaf axils, June-August (Burke); in the Olympics' late-melting snow basins July-August. The template's own generated record carries Sierra gooseberry's deciduous leaf_on_by_month (bare in winter) although its card is evergreen; this card sets leaf_on_by_month to 1 all year so the error does not carry over, and phyllodoce_breweri's card should do the same. Grows with white mountain heather (cassiope_mertensiana) and Cascade blueberry, and hybridises with yellow mountain heath (P. glanduliflora). No animal in the library eats it; bumblebees pollinate it, and mountain goats (introduced) and elk trample the heath.
